about: Tide stations for Northern Ireland's coast, which no Marine Institute station predicts (the foil-depth regions stop 45 km from the last of them). Each is EOT20 at the point (Hart-Davis et al. 2021, DGFI-TUM, CC BY 4.0). Where an open gauge is there (UK National Tide Gauge Network via the Copernicus Marine in-situ TAC, served on EMODnet Physics' ERDDAP), the model is fitted to it (timing, scale, datum) and the gauge's own levels are used when it has them; elsewhere the model's own Lowest Astronomical Tide (the lowest level it predicts over 19 years) is the datum. A pixel goes to one of these only if no Marine Institute station is within 45 km, so the Republic's regions are cut exactly as the foil-depth layer's.
basins: A station with a polygon (Strangford Lough, behind the Narrows) is its parent's tide (lagOf) lagMinutes later, the lag read off the imagery by lag.py (Strangford: 100 min, median misfit 0.065 against 0.26 on Killard's own timing); it takes every pixel in its polygon and none outside.
